execution.local_checks: count-control C++ tests, five analysis rejection tests, and 105 actual engine window-selection cases over seven circuits passed; new binary built; existing binary hashes unchanged
execution.previous_interactive_failure: QOSMaxSubmitJobPerUserLimit; interactive MaxSubmitJobsPU=2, both occupied by non-pp_ jobs

purpose: Test whether online sector-count adaptation reduces end-to-end time relative to fixed granularity, including the fastest tested fixed setting for each workload.
claim_boundary: This isolates sector-count adaptation. It does not establish that eight-candidate competition is a major speedup or independently establish novelty.

controls.overflow_splitting: Enabled identically in every policy; never disable the safety mechanism to make fixed-count controls fail.

fixed_control_semantics.bootstrap: Use the unchanged adaptive policy until it first requests at least 16 sector labels. From that decision onward request the specified constant number, including later shrinking windows. A workload that never triggers keeps the shared bootstrap, and is reported as no fixed-policy activation.
fixed_control_semantics.why_bootstrap: Avoid penalizing fixed controls for dividing the initial single Pauli term into many empty labels.
fixed_control_semantics.limits: Requested rows are capped by the actual annihilator dimension. Record requested labels, row rank, actual nonempty sectors, and emergency splits separately.
fixed_control_semantics.activation_audit: Before activation all policies must have matching windows, rows and input counts for the same policy seed. Reject an unmatched block for causal comparison.
fixed_control_semantics.meaning_of_fixed: Constant requested boundary sector count after shared bootstrap, with unchanged emergency splitting. This is not the existing fixed-rows ablation.

required_implementation_before_execution: Add a distinct fixed-sector-count control at gWanted selection; changing gmax or per-gpu is insufficient.

Decouple policy randomness from circuit seed. Use deterministic per-window and per-candidate random streams keyed by policy seed and window start, with a common candidate prefix and a separate spare-row stream.
Retain the existing RNG behavior as the default compatibility mode. The new matched-stream mode is experimental and must be explicit in all new comparisons.
Build a new binary manually, without the root build script and without replacing pp_engine_x or queued campaign binaries.
Record source commit, source diff if any, binary hash, full arguments, allocation, host list, policy seed and run order.

Verify the untouched default mode against pp_engine_x on all seven small-cutoff cases, checking answers, window boundaries and row-count traces. These are correctness/compatibility checks, not new performance results.

Verify fixed counts activate as specified and that all policies preserve window boundaries, truncation positions and answers. Record differences caused by unavoidable numerical effects rather than hiding them.

pilot.selection_reason: Predeclared representatives: standard KI, a different interaction graph, and the largest measured term population with stronger sector imbalance. All seven circuits remain in the confirmatory matrix.
pilot.decision: Not executed. Replaced by correctness-only validation followed directly by the predeclared confirmatory matrix, regardless of measured speedup.

validation.gate: All six policies must complete and preserve expectation, window schedule, shared bootstrap and prescribed count semantics. Compare the matched adaptive answer with the legacy reference. Do not gate continuation on timings or speedup.

execution_flow.sequence: One warmup, seven legacy pairs, and seven all-policy correctness blocks on each allocation, followed immediately by remaining confirmatory blocks.
execution_flow.continuation: Submit at most one four-node regular successor with afterany dependency on the current allocation after a normal time-budget exit. Retain one global loop lock and one allocation lock. Stop on correctness errors, source/hash mismatches, submission ambiguity, or the allocation limit.
execution_flow.resume: Skip only six-member confirmatory blocks already fully attempted in one allocation. Preserve failures as outcomes. Remeasure all six members of partial blocks together; never merge partial blocks across allocations.

confirmatory.uncertainty_scope: Five paired blocks vary policy randomness and execution noise together; do not describe this as five timing repeats at one policy seed or cross-allocation robustness.
confirmatory.ordering: For each policy seed, deterministically shuffle all 21 workloads, then shuffle the six policies in each workload using the logged schedule seed and block key. Keep the full block on the same allocation and warm each node's GPU/library path before measurement.
confirmatory.time_estimate_caveat: This is 775.22 seconds for the 21 existing adaptive runs times 6 policies times 5 blocks. It excludes warmup, launches and all static-policy slowdowns. Use prior adaptive times and observed full-block timings for admission. Completion in one four-hour allocation is not expected.
confirmatory.allocation_end_policy: Admit whole blocks using prior and observed times with a cleanup reserve. Preserve partial blocks as incomplete and remeasure all six members together in a dependent continuation. Do not combine a new control with an old allocation's variant.

secondary: actual sector labels and occupied sectors by window
measurements.instrumentation: Use existing counters for the primary timing campaign. Add detailed diagnostic counters in a separate explicit trace mode, held identical for all variants. Avoid extra per-window collectives or per-sector logging in the primary timed path.
mechanism_checks: If a coarse fixed count loses, check whether GPU/host splitting or worker idle actually increases.
If a fine fixed count loses, check whether tiny tasks, library calls or partition/copy costs actually increase.
If adaptive runtime falls without the proposed counters changing, report the observed effect without claiming that causal explanation.
Do not sum overlapping CPU and GPU counters as a wall-time decomposition.
measurements.answer_gate: Require the existing absolute expectation tolerance of 1e-9, and matching prescribed truncation/window schedules. Treat violations as invalid, never as performance wins.
measurements.failure_reporting: Keep OOM, timeout, invalid and unattempted runs distinct. Never assign an arbitrary large time or infinite speedup to them.

analysis.ordinary_reference: Fixed 16 labels after shared bootstrap, corresponding to one nominal task per GPU.
analysis.strong_reference: For each of the 21 workloads, the fastest tested fixed value among 16/32/64/128/256 according to its five-block mean. Disclose that this is a retrospective reference with workload-specific tuning, not a deployable oracle or a globally optimal fixed count.
analysis.ratios: Mean reference wall time divided by mean adaptive wall time, within each workload. Report all 21 results, including slowdowns.
analysis.aggregate: Equal-weight geometric mean across the 21 workloads, separately for fixed16 and best tested fixed. Also report each circuit and cutoff, win/loss counts and worst slowdown.
analysis.uncertainty: Paired bootstrap over the five seed/run blocks, retaining the six policies jointly. For an aggregate interval, resample the same seed blocks jointly across all 21 workloads to preserve seed dependence. Re-select the best tested fixed policy within each bootstrap replicate. Report descriptive ranges as well as the interval and disclose the small sample count.
analysis.practical_claim_gate: Use 10 percent as a predeclared practical aggregate target, with an interval lower bound above one. This is not a guarantee or a significance claim for every individual workload. Gains only against fixed16 do not support superiority over a tuned fixed policy.
analysis.if_small_or_negative: Do not change the cutoff/seed suite to obtain wins. Keep this as parameter robustness or tuning-avoidance evidence if justified, and lower the standalone performance claim. Preserve the existing candidate-selection result.
